# 1500 W Wilson Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN: 14171060250000 | Uptown (Community Area 3)**

---

## 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B1-2** — a Neighborhood Shopping District at the "-2" intensity level. This comes directly from the City's official GIS parcel database. You can verify it on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) by searching the PIN or address.

**Confidence:** High — this is an authoritative parcel-level match (not interpolated).

---

## 2. Residential Uses: Apartments Above and On Ground Floor

**Apartments above ground-floor retail:** Yes, mixed-use buildings with residential above ground-floor commercial are a standard permitted use in B1 districts. B1 is a neighborhood shopping district that explicitly contemplates ground-floor retail with upper-floor residential.

**Apartments on the ground floor:** This is more restricted. [5] establishes that in B and C districts, any new construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA or Metra rail station must satisfy specific transit-served location criteria — and separately, ground-floor residential conversion of a commercial space is possible but requires Zoning Administrator approval under a specific pathway [4]. Under [4], the Zoning Administrator is authorized to approve conversion of an occupied or vacant commercial establishment located *below the second floor* within a multi-story building into residential dwelling units. Standalone ground-floor residential in a new B1 building is generally not the permitted baseline use — retail/commercial is expected at grade.

**Confidence:** Moderate-high on the mixed-use principle; moderate on ground-floor residential — the specific B1 use table was not returned in this context, so the exact permitted/special use designation for ground-floor dwelling units should be confirmed against the B1 use table in Chapter 17-3. Verify at the Chicago Zoning Map or by contacting the Department of Planning and Development (DPD).

---

## 3. Bulk and Density Standards

The **zone_definition** data was not returned for this parcel's B1-2 classification, so I cannot state the specific numeric FAR cap, maximum height, minimum lot area per dwelling unit, or setbacks directly from code lookup results. What the code chunks do confirm:

- **FAR increase for transit-served locations:** [4] provides that projects in **B-3 and C-3** districts within 2,640 feet of a CTA or Metra rail station may increase their maximum FAR — but this specific bonus is tied to B-3/C-3, not B1-2. For B1-2, the base FAR and any transit-adjacent bonus must be verified against Table 17-3-0403-A and the B1-2 row specifically.
- **Average dwelling unit size (D districts):** [1] sets a minimum average of **500 sq ft gross residential floor area per dwelling unit** — note this section applies to Downtown (D) districts, not B districts, so it is cited for reference only and may not directly govern this parcel.
- **On-site open space (D districts):** [1] requires at least **36 sq ft of usable open space per dwelling unit** in D districts — again, cited for reference; B-district open space requirements would need separate verification.

**What I could not determine:** The specific B1-2 FAR limit, maximum building height, minimum lot area per dwelling unit, front/rear/side setback standards, and lot coverage maximum. These are in Table 17-3-0403-A and the B1-2 bulk standards table in [4] / Chapter 17-3-0400, but the numeric values were not returned in this context.

**How to verify:** Search "17-3-0403" and "17-3-0200" in the [Chicago Municipal Code online](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/provdrs/zon.html), or contact DPD's Zoning Help Desk at (312) 744-5777.

---

## 4. Overlays and Special Designations

This parcel carries **five regulatory overlays**:

- **Transit-Oriented Development — CTA:** The parcel is within the TOD overlay triggered by CTA rail proximity. The nearest CTA station is **Montrose (Brown Line)** at 0.45 miles. TOD overlay status is also confirmed for **Metra** (Ravenswood station, Union Pacific North Line, 0.39 miles away). Under the Connected Communities Ordinance, TOD eligibility enables density bonuses and reduced parking requirements near transit. [5] specifies that new construction within **2,640 feet** of a CTA or Metra rail entrance must comply with transit-served location criteria including pedestrian-street design standards.

- **ADU Eligible Area:** This parcel falls within an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) eligible area, meaning that if a residential building is established here, ADUs (coach houses or interior units) may be permissible subject to the ADU ordinance rules.

- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone:** Any residential development requiring a zoning entitlement (map amendment, planned development, or ARO-triggering approval) will be subject to affordable unit set-asides under the ARO [4][5]. Uptown already has 20 ARO/affordable housing projects totaling **976 units** across the community area, including projects like the Ruth Shriman House (231 senior units), Leland Apts. (137 units), and Harold Washington Apts. (100 supportive units).

- **Special Service Area — Greater Ravenswood (SSA):** This parcel lies within the Greater Ravenswood Special Service Area. SSA levies a supplemental tax on properties within the district to fund local commercial corridor services (streetscaping, marketing, etc.). Note this is reflected in the tax breakdown — the City of Chicago Special Service Area 31 levy accounts for ~$395/year in the estimated tax bill.

- **No Planned Development, Landmark, Historic District, Lakefront Protection, or PMD overlays apply.**

---

## 5. Parking Requirements and Transit-Related Reductions

The specific B1-2 parking table was not returned in this context, so I cannot state the baseline parking ratio (spaces per dwelling unit or per 1,000 sq ft of commercial). However:

- The **TOD overlay** (both CTA and Metra) is confirmed [5], and under the Connected Communities Ordinance, TOD-eligible projects within the applicable distance thresholds qualify for **reduced or eliminated parking minimums**. [5] specifies that new construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA or Metra rail station entrance must meet transit-served location standards.
- Given that the Ravenswood Metra station is **0.39 miles (~2,059 feet)** away and the Montrose Brown Line is **0.45 miles (~2,376 feet)** away, both are within the 2,640-foot threshold. This strongly positions the project for TOD parking reductions.

**What I could not determine:** The exact baseline parking ratio for B1-2 and the precise reduction percentage or elimination threshold under the Connected Communities Ordinance for this specific configuration. Verify in Chapter 17-10 of the Municipal Code and with DPD.

---

## 6. Maximum Height, FAR, and Transit Density Provisions

| Parameter | What I Can Confirm | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Base FAR (B1-2) | Not returned — verify Table 17-3-0403-A | [4] |
| FAR bonus (transit) | Available in **B-3/C-3** districts within 2,640 ft of rail via Type 1 amendment or PD | [4] |
| Max height (B1-2) | Not returned — verify Chapter 17-3-0400 | [4] |
| TOD parking reduction | Applicable — both CTA and Metra thresholds met | [5], overlay data |
| ARO trigger | Yes — any entitlement triggers affordable set-aside | [4][5] |

**Key transit/density insight:** The FAR increase specifically enumerated in [4] is for B-3 and C-3 districts. For a **B1-2** parcel, any density increase above the base FAR would likely require a **Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment** (rezoning to a higher B classification or to a planned development) rather than being available by-right.
